# Read this first

This is the living project reference. It describes the repository, not a claim
that every implemented feature has passed live commissioning. It is an R Markdown
document containing ordinary Markdown; reading it requires no R runtime. Optional
HTML rendering requires R and rmarkdown, which are not required by the application.

**Current network: Bitcoin Signet. Mainnet is disabled. Do not send real BTC.**
The owner has acknowledged test mode. A running deployment, a QR code, a successful
build and a healthy node do not establish real-money custody readiness.

Evidence labels used here:

- **Source:** implemented or configured in the repository.
- **Local check:** a local validation result, not proof of the deployed environment.
- **Owner-confirmed:** reported by the owner, not independently repeated by an agent.
- **Screenshot:** visible in supplied screenshots; a point-in-time observation.
- **Pending:** not established by the available evidence.

# Product and scope

Single-owner, self-hosted Bitcoin vault with a responsive web interface. The
project uses React/TypeScript and Node.js/Express for the website and API, and Go
for the private Bitcoin engine. C# is not part of the current implementation.
AWS is the host for Coolify, not an application integration with AWS managed
services. Cloudflare D1 remains the production metadata store.

The interface includes a portfolio overview, cold and spending wallets, temporary
receiving wallets, receiving QR codes, transactions, payment review, node explorer,
market/alerts and operational settings. The explorer uses the owner's node rather
than requiring a public block explorer. The existence of a screen does not mean
its external service is configured.

## Owner requirements

- No username/password account system: use a manually saved random owner key and
  enrolled passkeys.
- Owner credential is 64 random bytes encoded as 86 unpadded base64url characters.
  Its SHA-256 verifier is 64 hexadecimal characters. These lengths describe
  different encodings/objects; they are not interchangeable credentials.
- Support many independent temporary receiving wallets; the batch UI supports up
  to 200 per request. Local regtest evidence includes 101 wallets; live scale
  readiness remains separate.
- Show timestamps, incoming transactions, pending/confirmed balances, and expiry.
- Temporary wallets expire after 120 hours (five days). Expiration is not proof
  of destruction and does not reclaim a remaining balance.
- Keep a clean, approachable mobile-wallet UI rather than an engineering console.
- Track real prices and market drops, not simulated prices or market manipulation.
- Keep this roadmap current when files are added, changed, renamed or removed.

# Architecture and trust boundaries

```text
Owner browser (HTTPS)
  -> Coolify website: React static assets + Express API
      -> Cloudflare D1: application metadata
      -> private vault-engine:9090 (matching service token)
          -> Bitcoin Core RPC (private network + cookie authentication)
          -> persistent signer journal and Core wallet storage
      -> optional market Worker (not currently established as live)

Optional health replication:
  signer -> authenticated HTTPS Worker -> bounded metadata replication
Optional encrypted recovery exports:
  operator-controlled offline tooling -> encrypted backup storage
```

The browser does not hold Core RPC credentials. Public cold descriptors identify
receiving destinations but do not authorize cold spending. The hot spending
wallet and temporary wallet keys belong to the Core/signer custody boundary.
D1 availability must not become the authority for Bitcoin signing correctness.
Never run two active signers against the same state.

# Application walkthrough

## Authentication and sessions

The lock page accepts a saved keyfile or pasted owner key. The server verifies
the credential against its verifier; the owner secret must not be placed in
source code, chat or this document. Passkey enrollment and login use WebAuthn.
Session handling includes origin/CSRF protections, expiration, revocation,
rate-limiting and security notification support. Logout clears protected client
state and handles an already-expired session as logged out.

**Owner-confirmed on 2026-10-14:** passkey sign-in is working on the deployed app.
This confirms the reported sign-in experience, not every enrollment, revocation,
cross-device or recovery scenario.

Changing the deployment origin can affect cookies and WebAuthn. Preserve a working
owner-key backup and verify origin/RP configuration before changing domains.

## Dashboard, receiving and temporary wallets

The overview polls balances and node readiness. Missing node data must not appear
as a fabricated balance. Wallet pages expose receipt, labels, details and batch
creation. The receive interface uses the server's receive result, QR encoding,
copy/share controls and network warnings.

Signet native SegWit addresses begin with `tb1`, but this prefix alone does not
uniquely distinguish Signet from all other Bitcoin test networks. The configured
node network is authoritative. Real Bitcoin mainnet must not be sent to the
current QR codes.

Creation is blocked while Core reports initial block download or blocks trail
headers. The current “disconnected” presentation can also mean reconciliation is
incomplete; it must not be mistaken for proof that network transport is broken.
After sync the engine attempts initialization/reconciliation of the cold and
spending wallets. Temporary wallets are independent from those two main wallets.

## Sending, sweeping and recovery

Payments have review/approval and durable transaction tracking. Signed transaction
identity is journaled before broadcast so ambiguous responses can be reconciled
instead of blindly creating a second payment. Replacement, eviction, conflict
and reorg handling are separate from “success”.

Temporary sweeps require at least three confirmations and fresh cold destinations.
Three confirmations reduce risk; they are not an absolute finality guarantee.
Cold spending requires signing outside this web application.

Sweeps default to paused and limits default to zero. Configure suitable positive
fee and exposure limits before deliberately enabling operations. Fee estimates
that are missing or exceed limits must not silently authorize a payment.

## Expiry and destruction

At five days, a temporary wallet is expired, not magically erased. The implementation
retains keys while funds, unsettled transactions or uncertainty remain. Actual key
destruction/history removal remains blocked because secure storage erasure has not
been verified. Manual deletion must not bypass those conditions.

Deleting local records does not remove public blockchain transactions. Core unload,
file deletion and volume deletion are not proof that copies disappeared from SSD,
snapshots, swap, journals or backups. A retained shared seed must not silently
regenerate supposedly destroyed wallets. Late deposits to old addresses remain
possible; there is no guaranteed maximum confirmation delay.

## Market and notifications

The Worker implements Kraken XBTUSD sampling and D1 price history, with freshness
checks and price-drop alerts. The latest dashboard screenshot shows the market
service disconnected. Verify provider terms and Worker configuration before
enabling market ingestion. Do not invent prices.

Mail/security-alert code and configuration are present; deployed delivery must be
verified separately. Do not infer working mail from a successful website build.

# Storage, backups and privacy

| Store | Purpose | Operational boundary |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Vault application metadata; migration includes `vault_state`, `prices`, `replica` | Production must not silently fall back to local SQLite |
| Development SQLite | Local metadata adapter | Not the deployed D1 database |
| Core data volume | Blockchain and wallet data | Persistent; do not delete to troubleshoot routine deployment errors |
| Signer volume | Durable state, payment intent and recovery information | Single-writer authority; protect against rollback |
| Core cookie volume | Local RPC authentication | Read-only in signer; never expose publicly |
| R2 / replication scaffolding | Encrypted backup destination / bounded health metadata | Live restoration and end-to-end binding checks remain pending |

The offline backup utility uses AES-256-GCM with an independent 32-byte backup
key. That key is not the owner login key or signer service token. Recovery exports
must exclude temporary wallets and the whole hot-wallet journal. An opaque
spending-wallet backup cannot be proven safe merely by validating its JSON wrapper.

Health replication is a bounded snapshot channel, not a complete audit trail:
intermediate health samples may be coalesced. Do not claim that its queue contains
wallet payment history or that it is a substitute for recovery backups.

# Deployment and configuration

## Website resource

Root `Dockerfile` builds the API and React app, then runs a non-root Node 24
container on port 3000. Its health check calls `/api/healthz`. Coolify routes the
public HTTPS website to this resource. Static files are served before SPA fallback.

Runtime configuration includes these **names only**:

- `NODE_ENV`, `PORT`, `PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, `BITCOIN_NETWORK`, `VAULT_STATIC_DIR`.
- `VAULT_OWNER_VERIFIER` — verifier only, never the raw owner credential.
- `VAULT_ENGINE_URL`, `VAULT_ENGINE_TOKEN` — private signer access.
- `CF_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CF_D1_DATABASE_ID`, `CF_API_TOKEN` — D1 access.
- `MARKET_WORKER_URL` — optional configured market service.
- `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`,
  `SECURITY_ALERT_FROM`, `SECURITY_ALERT_TO`, `TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS` — mail/proxy configuration.

`deploy/app-config.mjs` and the environment examples remain authoritative for exact
validation requirements. Do not copy real values into documentation.

## Separate Bitcoin stack

- Build pack: Docker Compose; branch: `main`; base directory: `/`.
- Compose file: `/deploy/coolify-bitcoin.compose.yaml`.
- Coolify resolves build contexts from the repository root through
  `--project-directory`; both build contexts must follow that convention.
- Core and signer run on the same host as the website with private networking.
- Owner screenshot established shared network `coolify`; verify again if moving hosts.
- Core uses an internal RPC network and an outbound peer network.
- Signer additionally joins the existing application network.
- No public domains or host port mappings for Core RPC or signer.
- Required runtime input names: `VAULT_ENGINE_TOKEN`, `COLD_DESCRIPTOR`,
  `COLD_DESCRIPTOR_SHA256`, `COOLIFY_NETWORK`.
- Existing website uses `VAULT_ENGINE_URL=http://vault-engine:9090` on the verified
  shared private network and the same signer token.
- Disable build-time availability for signer credentials. Do not bake them into images.
- Core's Compose health check stays enabled. Do not add an unauthenticated HTTP
  check to the signer's protected `/status` endpoint.
- “Healthy” means the health probe passed; it does not mean initial sync finished.

Core is pinned to 29.0 for the current test deployment with a tarball checksum.
Reassess maintenance/security versions before any mainnet deployment; a checksum
check is not a claim of an independent release-signature verification.

## Setup generators

`public/offline-keygen.html` is for owner credentials. The Signet generator's source
is in `scripts/signet-setup-generator.mjs` plus its HTML template; the build script
produces `public/signet-setup.html` and an excluded downloadable copy.

The owner chose HTTPS on-device generation for a disposable Signet wallet because
the phone's downloaded-file preview did not run it. The page generates locally,
requires saving a private backup before showing deployment variables, and is not
a mainnet cold-wallet ceremony. The temporary homepage buttons were removed after
the owner obtained the setup. The HTML file remains present.

## Release and rollback discipline

Validate first, inspect changes, fetch GitHub, preserve existing history and use a
normal fast-forward push. Do not force-push or expose deploy private keys. A push is
not proof of a successful Coolify rollout. Observe runtime logs after deployment.
Never remove persistent wallet volumes as a casual rollback strategy.

# Roadmap and acceptance criteria

## Owner's current release order

The owner has now requested the mainnet/production transition. Real Bitcoin
receiving and sending are the immediate goal; this is authorization to prepare
that transition, not evidence that mainnet is enabled or verified.
Keep this phase focused without adding unrelated access friction. Retain essential
network, authentication, transaction-integrity and readiness safeguards.

A public API with rate limiting is explicitly deferred until the owner has
confirmed real-Bitcoin receiving and sending work. The owner will explain its
operating model later. Do not expose the private signer or Core RPC as that API.
Mainnet cold-wallet custody/export compatibility must be established before
choosing the migration configuration; never request a seed or private key in chat.

The owner selected **Trust Wallet** for mainnet savings. Its official receiving
guide documents selecting the asset and copying its receive address/QR:
<https://support.trustwallet.com/en/articles/717107-how-to-receive-cryptocurrency-in-trust-wallet-a-step-by-step-guide>.
An official public-descriptor/xpub export procedure has not been established by
this review. A fixed native-Bitcoin destination is a possible adaptation, not
implemented or approved yet. It reuses an address, reducing privacy; Trust Wallet
on a connected phone is not offline cold storage. Keep control of its private
keys in Trust Wallet rather than importing them into the vault server.

## 1. Finish hosted Signet commissioning

- Demonstrate temporary-wallet creation and persistence across a controlled restart.
- Receive test coins and show pending -> confirmed transitions from this node.
- Review/send once, confirm on-chain, and demonstrate safe duplicate handling.
- Configure positive fee/exposure limits deliberately; exercise sweeps at three
  confirmations and confirm destination/accounting.
- Exercise unavailable-node behavior, recovery and restored-wallet reconciliation
  with disposable test funds and preserved backups.
- Retain passkey owner confirmation; separately verify revocation, expiry,
  logout across tabs and account-recovery paths if those behaviors change.
- Improve status labels so transport connectivity and wallet readiness are distinct.

## 2. Finish external services and recovery evidence

- Commission market Worker only after provider/configuration approval.
- Verify alert delivery and clear failure reporting.
- Verify live D1/R2/Worker/replication bindings, authentication and outage replay.
- Perform an actual encrypted recovery round trip and restore reconciliation.

## 3. Mainnet migration — explicit separate release

- Review custody/security assumptions and maintained dependency/Core versions.
- Introduce consistent mainnet configuration across API, signer, UI and validators.
- Provision separate mainnet storage and a verified receiving descriptor from the
  owner's backed-up wallet, preferably hardware-backed for cold custody.
- Never reuse the disposable web-generated Signet private backup for mainnet custody.
- Synchronize mainnet and validate readiness; do not bypass syncing gates.
- Verify small controlled receive/send/recovery behavior before meaningful funds.
- Keep clear network labels and QR validation; changing wording is not migration.

## 4. Destruction policy implementation

Retain disabled destruction until an approved independent key lifecycle and copy
inventory can support verifiable erasure. Define late-deposit handling and irreversible
loss consequences. Blockchain history cannot be erased by this application.

# Developer workflow and verification

```sh
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm --filter @workspace/api-spec run codegen
bash scripts/vault-verify.sh
node scripts/build-signet-generator.mjs
node scripts/update-roadmap.mjs
node scripts/update-roadmap.mjs --check
```

Run codegen only when changing the API contract, and rebuild the Signet HTML after
editing its generator/template. The broad verification script covers types,
Node/API/frontend utility tests, deployment packaging and Go checks. Inspect its
current contents for the exact suite. Regtest and container probes are local
evidence, not replacements for hosted commissioning.

Documentation-only work should validate documentation/inventory, not unnecessarily
restart services or run real payment flows. No new live-payment evidence is claimed
by this roadmap update.

# Continuous documentation contract

For every codebase update:

1. Update the relevant narrative sections, status evidence, configuration and tests.
2. Refresh the inventory with `node scripts/update-roadmap.mjs`.
3. Review its added/changed/removed list. Confirm that exclusions are intentional.
4. Run `node scripts/update-roadmap.mjs --check` before release.
5. Keep pending work pending until evidence supports completion.

The script enumerates tracked plus non-ignored untracked project files, excludes
private/tool-generated locations, and records file size and SHA-256 content
fingerprints. The document's own fingerprint normalizes the generated inventory
section to avoid a self-referential hash. Changes to the narrative are still detected.
This is an inventory freshness check, not an automatic semantic code reviewer.
Purpose summaries are indexed roles, not a claim that every line was manually audited.

Never inventory actual secrets, `.env` values, private keys, wallet backups, database
contents, installed dependencies or local tool state. Uploaded evidence is listed
by filename only; its text/images are not copied into the roadmap.

## Excluded file classes

`.git`, `.local`, `.cache`, `.config`, `node_modules`, build output, caches, generated
exports, temporary logs, secret files and wallet/database state are excluded.
Tracked source-generated clients and the public bundled Signet page remain included.
Ignored uploads are outside the version-controlled handoff; tracked uploads remain
listed as evidence assets. Filenames are not evidence that an attachment is safe
to publish: review repository assets before release.
